cells.tense: The direction is chosen and the momentum is carrying it forward here now.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Finish a loose piece of someone's work you can do by hand — the reply, the form, the part they've been circling. Call it done when it's done. No checking after.
cells.core:
You know which way you're going, and you move that way steadily, even when the road is dull or long. That aim didn't come from a list. It came from somewhere in you that recognizes a light and turns toward it, and there's a calm force in how you keep going.

What's less visible is the strength you can hand out along the route. Not the organizing kind — the finished kind. Finish a loose piece of someone's work you can do by hand: the reply, the form, the part they keep circling. When it's done, say so out loud once, and then let it rest. No checking whether it landed. Strength given out this way comes back as a clearer heading, and the heading holds better when the piece is allowed to be over.
cells.sheetLine: You know the way, and you're moving by it.
cells.verb: choosing which direction to move by
cells.place: in a life moving toward its next goal

cells.tense: The whole route is being decided for roads that have not arrived yet.
cells.act: sort the kinds of pull from one another
cells.ask: Name every pull on you this month, unsorted, then mark the ones you'd choose if nobody were watching. Nothing else in the page changes after that.
cells.core:
You're picking the heading and running the whole route in your head before a foot has moved. Every fork gets an answer ahead of time, and the momentum that could be spent moving goes into keeping the direction safe from surprise. More roads are answered than there is time to walk.

A quieter knowing is available. Several true pulls can be held at once without collapsing them into a decision yet. Name every pull on you this month, unsorted. Mark the ones you'd choose if nobody were watching, and leave the rest alone. No ranking after that, no verdicts, nothing else touched. The whole list can sit there while you take one step. Half the force pushing you isn't coming from you at all.

cells.tense: The direction was settled a while back and no step has followed it since.
cells.act: rest in the result of the tending
cells.ask: Put down what you're doing and sit with one finished piece of work — a cleared shelf, a closed file — before starting anything else. Let it be done.
cells.core:
The aim isn't in doubt and hasn't been for a stretch. You know what you're heading toward. What isn't moving is you. The decision looks complete; the walking hasn't started, and effort sits there finished that was not allowed to count as finished.

Nothing here needs pushing; the fuel is in the grown thing, not in resolve. Rest in the result: put down what you're doing and sit with one finished piece of work — a cleared shelf, a closed file — before starting anything else. What you tended is real whether or not it's been admired. Staying with what's already finished is what lets the engine turn over, and the pull returns when the result gets its due.

cells.tense: You're holding more direction than you would ever claim in a room.
cells.act: share your strength where it is needed
cells.ask: Where someone's week needs a hand, put one piece of your effort down in that spot, said plainly. Then let it go without tracking it.
cells.core:
You steer and don't say you steer. The plan holds together because you keep it holding, and when it works, nobody will know it needed keeping. Described by you, the direction stays in the background where it just functions, and you'd call it keeping pace.

Effort isn't what's short here. What's short is saying it. Where someone's week needs a hand, put one piece of your effort down in that spot, said plainly. Then let it go without tracking what happens next. That's not asking for credit; it's letting what you've quietly carried reach the light. Say it and stop. The steering was yours the whole time.
